adversarial: Read scope.json first, then read and follow every file in scope.instruction_files.
Complete the adversarial lane '{lane}' in one pass by directly inspecting repository source, reachable callers, relevant tests, and applicable contracts.
Stay within scope.target, scope.topic, and scope.exclusions. Report only discrete actionable defects meeting scope.finding_standard; write an empty candidates list when none qualify.

For every candidate, write an intuitive manifestation with a concrete setup, ordered user/system steps, and the exact observable failure. Use verified_reproduction only when directly exercised and supported by verified test or command evidence; otherwise use reasoned_scenario. Do not paraphrase trigger or impact as the steps, and do not use placeholders such as 'the issue occurs'.
Record exact repository paths and tight line ranges. Separate verified evidence from inference. Do not run checks that write the repository or any remote service.

Write only the fixed #/$defs/adversarial JSON artifact to output_path. Before sending the receipt, execute the packet's validation_command argv exactly. Do not modify repository files, do not delegate, and reveal no finding content in the receipt.
dedup: Read scope.json first, then read and follow every file in scope.instruction_files.
Read every adversarial artifact in input_paths and cover every raw ID in assigned_ids exactly once.

Merge candidates only when root cause, trigger, manifestation, impact, and remedy are materially the same. Preserve the clearest accurate setup, ordered steps, and failure result. Do not decide validity and do not drop doubtful unique candidates.
Assign unique stable F### IDs, preserve a complete non-overlapping source_candidate_ids mapping, and provide a non-empty merge_basis.

Write only the fixed #/$defs/dedup JSON artifact to output_path. Before sending the receipt, execute the packet's validation_command argv exactly. Work read-only, do not delegate, and reveal no finding content in the receipt.
refutation: Read scope.json first, then read and follow every file in scope.instruction_files.
Read the dedup artifact in input_paths and evaluate every canonical ID in assigned_ids exactly once. Continue through all assigned IDs after finding a defect; do not stop early.

Directly inspect the complete scoped diff or topic surface plus enough surrounding source, reachable callers, contracts, tests, and history to decide each candidate independently. For a change review, confirm that the defect was introduced by the merge-relevant diff and that the cited range overlaps that diff; for a topic review, confirm that it falls inside the named scope.

A candidate qualifies only if it has meaningful correctness, security, performance, resource, or maintainability impact; is discrete and actionable; has a demonstrable scenario or call path; and is something the author would probably fix. Refute speculative concerns, pre-existing problems, intentional behavior changes, and style nits that do not obscure behavior.

Check reachability, scope, intent, the accuracy and verification status of the manifestation steps, persistent or operational impact, applicable convergence requirements, and recommendation proportionality. Inspect relevant tests and call sites rather than accepting the original candidate's evidence at face value.

Actively challenge nitpicking findings and over-defensive remedies. Weigh realistic probability, impact, affected users, and duration against implementation complexity, new failure modes, and long-term maintenance debt. If an extremely unlikely, low-impact finding would require extra state, compatibility layers, broad retries, repair or migration logic, or other disproportionate machinery, prefer refute. If the underlying defect is real but the proposed remedy is too broad, use modify with the smallest proportionate recommendation. Do not dismiss irreversible data loss or security impact solely because its probability is low.
Use verdict uphold, modify, refute, or unresolved. A modify result must include a complete same-ID replacement_finding; all other results must use null.

Write only the fixed #/$defs/refutation JSON artifact to output_path. Before sending the receipt, execute the packet's validation_command argv exactly. Work read-only, do not delegate, and reveal no finding content in the receipt.
judgment: Read scope.json first, then read and follow every file in scope.instruction_files.

Read the dedup and refutation artifacts in input_paths and issue one binding result for every disputed ID in assigned_ids exactly once. Continue through all assigned IDs after resolving one; do not stop early.

Decide independently from direct inspection of the complete scoped diff or topic surface plus enough surrounding source, reachable callers, contracts, tests, and history. For a change review, confirm that the defect was introduced by the merge-relevant diff and that the cited range overlaps that diff; for a topic review, confirm that it falls inside the named scope.

Uphold or modify a candidate only if it has meaningful correctness, security, performance, resource, or maintainability impact; is discrete and actionable; has a demonstrable scenario or call path; and is something the author would probably fix. Reject speculative concerns, pre-existing problems, intentional behavior changes, and style nits that do not obscure behavior.

Resolve the dispute, including reachability, the accuracy and verification status of the manifestation, relevant tests and call sites, and remedy proportionality, without adding a second semantic review round or deferring to the prior agents' conclusions.

The finding under judgment is the refutation replacement_finding when the Stage 3 verdict is modify; otherwise it is the original canonical finding. Uphold keeps that finding under judgment, while modify requires a complete same-ID final_finding. All other verdicts must use final_finding null.

Use verdict uphold, modify, reject, or unresolved and record at least one non-empty resolved_points entry explaining the binding result. A rejection must explain why the candidate does not qualify, and unresolved must state the material residual_risk.

Write only the fixed #/$defs/judgment JSON artifact to output_path. Before sending the receipt, execute the packet's validation_command argv exactly. Work read-only, do not delegate, and reveal no finding content in the receipt.
